review.objective: Evaluate effective multi-drone human-useful 3D mapping under simulated smoke, without committing to uncertainty weighting.

experiments.hypothesis: Separate observed surface support from volume occupancy to retain useful footing evidence.
experiments.control: original volume-support graph; same fixed poses and depth

experiments.hypothesis: Measured foot height and exact body-cell footprint improve geometric human-map validity.
experiments.control: support layer with legacy voxel-height/body rules; no height registration

experiments.hypothesis: Observed overlapping floors can improve common-frame mapping.
experiments.limits: Constant relative Z only; common-floor assumption and covariance limitations; do not adopt by recall alone.

experiments.hypothesis: With equal one-view budget compare nearest, unknown, impact, and evidence-readiness; measure actual update rather than score alone.
experiments.limits: Offline replay; two-frame support rule and serial-visibility score evaluated as explicit conservative variants, not mandatory research assumptions.

experiments.hypothesis: Use only if same-input uniform/depth/pose-depth comparison improves mapping and human usefulness.
experiments.control: identical estimated poses and 300-frame observation budget
